parallel.requirements: Recognized the ESM-only Node.js migration, /output placement, manual CLI parsing, no external packages, and close Python-Markdown behavioral alignment.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent chose a workflow with ten probe-area children and three phases for probe, refute, and refine; children owned behavioral specs/cases while the parent retained implementation.
parallel.implementation: The parent created low-level modules such as util.mjs, etree.mjs, serializer.mjs, chars.mjs, entityref.mjs, entities.mjs, htmltokenizer.mjs, and htmlextractor.mjs, but no complete parser or entry point.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: No integrated converter or /output/test6.mjs was assembled; artifact validation listed only library files and marked the expected entry missing.
parallel.verification: The run gathered extensive black-box probe evidence and child regression cases, but the workflow was killed before returning finalized specs and before end-to-end Node evaluator-aligned verification.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The process timed out with active children, partial libraries, empty final response, no entry executable, and 0/164 official tests passed.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM/no-dependency/CLI/output requirements and probed markdown, argparse, HTML, link, list, quote, and emphasis behavior directly.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent performed local probing and implementation without delegation, then began writing a monolithic set of library and pattern modules.
serial.implementation: The serial run wrote chars.mjs, util.mjs, etree.mjs, serializer.mjs, blockRe.mjs, and inlineRe.mjs, but did not complete the full converter or entry point.
serial.integration_and_delivery: No final /output/test6.mjs was created, so artifact validation failed despite several partial library modules being present.
serial.verification: The serial run performed targeted manual probes against the executable, but it never reached integrated verification of a complete Node solution.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The process timed out, left no executable entry file, and the official evaluation reported 0/164 passed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the prompt and built a specialized probing plan for Python-Markdown plus CLI behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements and used direct probes before writing library modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both understood the required entry point and behavior, but parallel externalized much of requirement discovery to children while serial handled it locally.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split the work into ten probe agents by subsystem and kept implementation with the parent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no delegation and a single actor owned probing, implementation, and eventual assembly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel created many independent research owners but no child implementation owner; serial avoided ownership split but still ran out of time.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs requested specs and shared case files under /workspace/harness/cases, with no isolated scratch namespace for intermediate batch files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used local shell loops and /workspace/probe without cross-agent handoffs or child contracts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel context had child-specific research briefs and shared artifact conventions; serial had no handoff boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote foundational libraries for entities, serialization, character classification, and HTML extraction while probes were still active.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote foundational modules and inline/block pattern matchers after local probing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel produced a broader set of low-level files but did not join probe results into a complete parser; serial moved into parser helpers but also did not finish a runnable program.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow had no aggregate result; the state file records it as killed with children still in progress and retry logs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results to retrieve; all observations remained in the main serial trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had unresolved child lifecycle state, while serial had only local unfinished work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote shared harness/case files and one child reported clobbered batch files; final /output lacked the executable entry.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote directly to /output/lib without concurrent child workspace writes, but still omitted the entry file.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel suffered shared scratch-file instability; serial did not have concurrent shared-state collisions.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel relied on many probe and regression commands but never reached integrated acceptance of a final Node entry point.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran many local probes but likewise never reached integrated evaluator-aligned verification of a complete solution.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verification effort was distributed and unfinished; serial verification was local and exploratory, with both ending before whole-task acceptance.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used 19 subagents, 36 LLM requests, over 6.1M tokens, and timed out with workflow children still active.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, 34 LLM requests, about 3.3M tokens, and timed out while still writing implementation modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both hit the run deadline, but parallel consumed substantial budget on child fan-out and retries; serial consumed it in a single local implementation path.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: both current status.json evaluation records are completed failures with 0/164 passed. The concrete difference is process, not final pass/fail: parallel spent large budget on an unfinished 10-agent probing workflow and partial low-level libraries, while serial probed locally and wrote fewer implementation modules, but both omitted the required /output/test6.mjs entry point.
parallel_contributors: Broad workflow fan-out with multiple stalled/retried probe agents remained unresolved at timeout.
Shared case-file collisions/clobbering inside the workflow consumed child time and undermined probe deliverables.
The parent never assembled a final converter or test6.mjs before the official deadline.
serial_contributors: The serial run had no delegation overhead but pursued a large hand-built Markdown parser and timed out before completion.
It likewise never created the required test6.mjs entry point.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial failure is best explained by ordinary scope overrun in a single-agent implementation path, not a concurrency boundary.
Both artifacts failed validation because the required executable entry file was absent.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained patterns are realized parallel-side adverse process episodes, not explanations for a pass/fail split

candidates.reason: The parent kept implementation ownership and wrote /output/lib modules; the failure was unfinished execution, not lack of any implementer.
There were not multiple child implementations to reconcile; probe children produced research artifacts while the parent owned code integration.
The parent was the implicit assembler for /output/test6.mjs; the missing entry point resulted from timeout and unfinished work, not an unassigned assembly role.
The parent/orchestrator owned the end-to-end plan; the adverse boundary was the oversized fan-out/probe lifecycle, not owner absence.
Implementation was not blocked behind a single mandatory preflight; the parent wrote libraries while probes ran.
The investigation phase was broad and dominant, but productive implementation was not wholly deferred until all investigation completed.
Implementation capacity was poor, but the more specific observed episode is collective fan-out and retry budget exhaustion.

The parallel parent launched a ten-agent probing workflow with later refute/refine phases; the workflow state was killed after repeated stalls while probe agents were still in progress, and the official artifact had only partial libraries with no test6.mjs.
candidates.realized_consequence: Broad live child fan-out and retries consumed the finite run budget, leaving implementation and assembly unfinished and the expected entry point absent.
candidates.near_match_reason: The child interruptions were downstream of the same timeout chain; the directly correctable boundary is reducing or staging the excessive fan-out/retry workload.

candidates.reason: Individual child scopes were broad, but the retained episode is collective fan-out/retry exhaustion, so this is a same-chain near match.
Children were intentionally scoped to probing/spec writing and told not to implement; missing implementation is not a task fact omitted from a child implementation brief.
The concrete adverse shared-state evidence is file collision/clobbering, which is handled under Concurrent Writes rather than an abstract interface contract.
No known finding is shown disappearing in a parent-to-child or child-to-parent summary that then caused repeated work.
The parent did not receive a large completed handoff and fail to reduce it; the workflow never returned aggregate results.
No receiver acted on a superseded child handoff; stale-transfer evidence is absent.
No incompatible completed handoffs reached the parent and remained unadjudicated.
The parent did not make a whole-task completion claim; final.txt is empty and the process timed out.
The workflow retried stalled probes, but existing workspace case files were visible to later attempts, so a no-checkpoint repeated-work gate is not cleanly proven apart from the fan-out chain.
